343 | def _to_sdk_content(blocks: list[RequestBlock]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
344 |     """Translate normalized request blocks → Anthropic wire-format block dicts.
345 | 
346 |     Byte-identical to the dicts the orchestrator constructed pre-refactor
347 |     (``TextBlock`` → ``{"type":"text","text"}``; ``ToolUseBlock`` →
348 |     ``{"type":"tool_use","id","name","input"}``; ``ToolResultBlock`` →
349 |     ``{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id","content"}``).
350 |     """
351 |     sdk_blocks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
352 |     for block in blocks:
353 |         if isinstance(block, TextBlock):
354 |             sdk_blocks.append({"type": "text", "text": block.text})
355 |         elif isinstance(block, ToolUseBlock):
356 |             sdk_blocks.append({
357 |                 "type": "tool_use",
358 |                 "id": block.id,
359 |                 "name": block.name,
360 |                 "input": block.input,
361 |             })
362 |         elif isinstance(block, ToolResultBlock):
363 |             sdk_blocks.append({
364 |                 "type": "tool_result",
365 |                 "tool_use_id": block.tool_use_id,
366 |                 "content": block.content,
367 |             })
368 |     return sdk_blocks
369 | 
370 | 
371 | def _to_sdk_messages(messages: list[Message]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
372 |     """Translate the normalized conversation → Anthropic ``messages`` wire format.
373 | 
374 |     ``Message.content: str`` (plain user prompts) stays a string content;
375 |     ``Message.content: list[RequestBlock]`` (assistant / tool-result turns)
376 |     becomes a list of block dicts. This preserves the exact shapes the
377 |     orchestrator built before P1-002.
378 |     """
379 |     sdk_messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
380 |     for msg in messages:
381 |         if isinstance(msg.content, str):
382 |             sdk_messages.append({"role": msg.role, "content": msg.content})
383 |         else:
384 |             sdk_messages.append({
385 |                 "role": msg.role,
386 |                 "content": _to_sdk_content(msg.content),
387 |             })
388 |     return sdk_messages

392 |     """Translate ``ToolDef`` → the ``{name, description, input_schema}`` dicts
393 |     the SDK expects (the pre-refactor ``AGENT_TOOLS`` shape)."""
394 |     return [
395 |         {
396 |             "name": tool.name,
397 |             "description": tool.description,
398 |             "input_schema": tool.input_schema,
399 |         }
400 |         for tool in tools
401 |     ]

404 | def _from_sdk_response(raw: Any) -> ProviderResponse:
405 |     """Translate a raw ``anthropic.types.Message`` → normalized ``ProviderResponse``.
406 | 
407 |     Enforces the R5 invariant: if any content block is a ``tool_use``, the
408 |     normalized ``stop_reason`` is ``TOOL_USE`` regardless of the native
409 |     ``stop_reason`` (Gemini reports ``STOP`` with function calls present;
410 |     defensive for all providers).
411 |     """
412 |     content: list[ContentBlock] = []
413 |     has_tool_use = False
414 |     for block in getattr(raw, "content", None) or []:
415 |         block_type = getattr(block, "type", None)
416 |         if block_type == "text":
417 |             content.append(TextBlock(text=block.text))
418 |         elif block_type == "tool_use":
419 |             has_tool_use = True
420 |             content.append(ToolUseBlock(
421 |                 id=block.id,
422 |                 name=block.name,
423 |                 input=dict(block.input) if not isinstance(block.input, dict) else block.input,
424 |             ))
425 | 
426 |     if has_tool_use:
427 |         stop_reason = StopReason.TOOL_USE
428 |     else:
429 |         raw_stop_reason = getattr(raw, "stop_reason", None)
430 |         stop_reason = (
431 |             _STOP_REASON_MAP.get(raw_stop_reason, StopReason.OTHER)
432 |             if isinstance(raw_stop_reason, str)
433 |             else StopReason.OTHER
434 |         )
435 | 
436 |     raw_usage = getattr(raw, "usage", None)
437 |     usage = Usage(
438 |         input_tokens=getattr(raw_usage, "input_tokens", 0) or 0,
439 |         output_tokens=getattr(raw_usage, "output_tokens", 0) or 0,
440 |     )
441 |     return ProviderResponse(
442 |         content=content,
443 |         stop_reason=stop_reason,
444 |         usage=usage,
445 |         raw_model=getattr(raw, "model", "") or "",
446 |     )
447 | 
448 | 
449 | _STOP_REASON_MAP: dict[str, StopReason] = {
450 |     "end_turn": StopReason.END_TURN,
451 |     "tool_use": StopReason.TOOL_USE,
452 |     "max_tokens": StopReason.MAX_TOKENS,
453 |     "stop_sequence": StopReason.STOP_SEQUENCE,
454 | }

457 | class AnthropicProvider:
458 |     """``LLMProvider`` adapter over the Anthropic SDK (ARC-011 P1-002).
459 | 
460 |     A 1:1 boundary translator: normalized ``Message``/``ToolDef``/``system``
461 |     become Anthropic ``messages.create`` kwargs (byte-identical to the
462 |     pre-refactor orchestrator call), and the raw ``anthropic.types.Message``
463 |     becomes a normalized ``ProviderResponse``. The provider owns no retry —
464 |     loop-owned retry (``orchestrator.py`` ``_call_llm_with_retry``) reads
465 |     ``classify_error`` and decides backoff + the budget-aware skip.
466 |     """
467 | 
468 |     name = "anthropic"
469 | 
470 |     def __init__(self, *, base_url: str, api_key: str, timeout_s: float) -> None:
471 |         # ``connect=30.0`` mirrors the pre-refactor orchestrator construction.
472 |         self._client = anthropic.AsyncAnthropic(
473 |             base_url=base_url,
474 |             api_key=api_key,
475 |             timeout=httpx.Timeout(timeout_s, connect=30.0),
476 |         )
477 | 
478 |     async def messages_create(
479 |         self,
480 |         *,
481 |         model: str,
482 |         system: str,
483 |         messages: list[Message],
484 |         tools: list[ToolDef],
485 |         max_tokens: int,
486 |         temperature: float | None = None,
487 |         stop_sequences: list[str] | None = None,
488 |     ) -> ProviderResponse:
489 |         """One model turn via ``messages.create`` (replaces the orchestrator call).
490 | 
491 |         ``temperature`` / ``stop_sequences`` are only forwarded when set — the
492 |         orchestrator never sets them today, so the wire request is unchanged.
493 |         """
494 |         kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
495 |             "model": model,
496 |             "max_tokens": max_tokens,
497 |             "system": system,
498 |             "tools": _to_sdk_tools(tools),
499 |             "messages": _to_sdk_messages(messages),
500 |         }
501 |         if temperature is not None:
502 |             kwargs["temperature"] = temperature
503 |         if stop_sequences is not None:
504 |             kwargs["stop_sequences"] = stop_sequences
505 |         raw = await self._client.messages.create(**kwargs)
506 |         return _from_sdk_response(raw)
507 | 
508 |     async def complete(
509 |         self,
510 |         *,
511 |         model: str,
512 |         prompt: str,
513 |         max_tokens: int,
514 |         system: str | None = None,
515 |     ) -> str:
516 |         """One-shot text completion (insights / Haiku path).
517 | 
518 |         Wraps the bare ``messages.create`` the orchestrator's
519 |         ``_extract_session_insights`` used: no tools, no retry, a single user
520 |         message. Returns only the joined text.
521 |         """
522 |         kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
523 |             "model": model,
524 |             "max_tokens": max_tokens,
525 |             "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
526 |         }
527 |         if system is not None:
528 |             kwargs["system"] = system
529 |         raw = await self._client.messages.create(**kwargs)
530 |         return "".join(
531 |             block.text for block in raw.content if getattr(block, "type", None) == "text"
532 |         )
533 | 
534 |     async def stream(self, **kwargs: Any) -> AsyncIterator[StreamDelta]:
535 |         """Token streaming (OPTIONAL in v1; D-stream). Not implemented for Anthropic."""
536 |         raise NotImplementedError(
537 |             "AnthropicProvider.stream is not implemented (ARC-011 D-stream)"
538 |         )
539 |         yield StreamDelta()  # pragma: no cover — makes this an async generator
540 | 
541 |     def estimate_cost(self, model: str, usage: Usage) -> float:
542 |         """Flat Sonnet-3.5-baseline USD cost (parity with pre-refactor accounting).
543 | 
544 |         Per-model pricing is P1-003; this preserves the cache-blind math the
545 |         orchestrator used before P1-002.
546 |         """
547 |         return (
548 |             usage.input_tokens * _CLAUDE_INPUT_USD_PER_TOKEN
549 |             + usage.output_tokens * _CLAUDE_OUTPUT_USD_PER_TOKEN
550 |         )
551 | 
552 |     def capabilities(self) -> ProviderCapabilities:
553 |         return ProviderCapabilities(
554 |             native_tool_use=True,
555 |             streaming=False,
556 |             system_prompt=True,
557 |             max_context_tokens=200_000,
558 |         )
559 | 
560 |     def classify_error(self, exc: Exception) -> ErrorClass:
561 |         """Classify an SDK exception for loop-owned retry.
562 | 
563 |         ``transient`` mirrors the pre-refactor ``_call_claude_with_retry``
564 |         decision: the three connection/timeout/server exception types, plus
565 |         ``APIStatusError`` with a status code in ``_TRANSIENT_STATUS_CODES``
566 |         (429 / 502 / 503 / 529). Everything else is non-transient.
567 |         """
568 |         if isinstance(
569 |             exc,
570 |             (
571 |                 anthropic.APITimeoutError,
572 |                 anthropic.APIConnectionError,
573 |                 anthropic.InternalServerError,
574 |             ),
575 |         ):
576 |             return ErrorClass(transient=True, status_code=None, retry_after_s=None)
577 |         if isinstance(exc, anthropic.APIStatusError):
578 |             status_code = getattr(exc, "status_code", None)
579 |             return ErrorClass(
580 |                 transient=status_code in _TRANSIENT_STATUS_CODES,
581 |                 status_code=status_code,
582 |                 retry_after_s=None,
583 |             )
584 |         return ErrorClass(transient=False, status_code=None, retry_after_s=None)

122 |         plus a non-empty ``approver``, ``signature``, and ``method`` so the

125 |         if (self.scope or "").lower() != "production":
126 |             return self

128 |         missing: list[str] = []
129 |         if approval is None:
130 |             missing.append("approval")
131 |         else:
132 |             if approval.approved is not True:
133 |                 missing.append("approval.approved=true")
134 |             for field_name in ("approver", "signature", "method"):
135 |                 value = getattr(approval, field_name, None)
136 |                 if not (isinstance(value, str) and value.strip()):
137 |                     missing.append(f"approval.{field_name}")
138 |         if missing:

154 | # W18 / P0-020: canonical message over which the approval HMAC signature is
155 | # computed. The operator (or UI) signs this exact string keyed by the
156 | # production_approval_verifier secret; the server re-derives and compares.
157 | _PRODUCTION_APPROVAL_MESSAGE_TEMPLATE = "{research_id}:{scope}:{approver}"
158 | 
159 | 
160 | def _verify_production_approval_signature(
161 |     research_id: str,
162 |     payload: PromotionScopeRequest,
163 | ) -> None:
164 |     """Cryptographically verify the production approval signature (W18).
165 | 
166 |     Layered AFTER ``PromotionScopeRequest._enforce_production_approval`` which
167 |     guarantees ``approval`` is present with non-empty ``approver``/``signature``
168 |     for ``scope=production``. Raises ``ValueError`` on (a) verifier unset
169 |     (fail-closed) or (b) signature mismatch, so the existing handler branch
170 |     maps it to HTTP 400 and records an audit failure.
171 |     """
172 |     verifier = secret_value(settings.production_approval_verifier)
173 |     if not verifier:
174 |         raise ValueError(
175 |             "production approval verifier is not configured "
176 |             "(AUTORESEARCH_PRODUCTION_APPROVAL_VERIFIER)"
177 |         )
178 |     approval = payload.approval
179 |     # The structural validator guarantees approval is present with non-empty
180 |     # approver/signature for scope=production; this guard exists for type
181 |     # safety and defense-in-depth (it is unreachable in normal flow).
182 |     if approval is None or not approval.approver or not approval.signature:
183 |         raise ValueError("production approval is missing required fields")
184 |     message = _PRODUCTION_APPROVAL_MESSAGE_TEMPLATE.format(
185 |         research_id=research_id,
186 |         scope=payload.scope,
187 |         approver=approval.approver,
188 |     ).encode("utf-8")
189 |     expected = hmac.new(
190 |         verifier.encode("utf-8"), message, hashlib.sha256
191 |     ).hexdigest()
192 |     provided = approval.signature.strip()
193 |     if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, provided):
194 |         raise ValueError("production approval signature rejected")

616 | def _to_openai_messages(
617 |     messages: list[Message], system: str,
618 | ) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
619 |     """Translate the normalized conversation → OpenAI Chat Completions messages.
620 | 
621 |     The Anthropic top-level ``system`` becomes a leading ``role:"system"``
622 |     message. Assistant turns carry ``tool_calls``; tool-result turns become
623 |     ``role:"tool"`` messages keyed by ``tool_call_id`` (one per result block).
624 |     """
625 |     oai_messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
626 |     if system:
627 |         oai_messages.append({"role": "system", "content": system})
628 |     for msg in messages:
629 |         if isinstance(msg.content, str):
630 |             oai_messages.append({"role": msg.role, "content": msg.content})
631 |             continue
632 |         if msg.role == "assistant":
633 |             text_parts: list[str] = []
634 |             tool_calls: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
635 |             for block in msg.content:
636 |                 if isinstance(block, TextBlock):
637 |                     text_parts.append(block.text)
638 |                 elif isinstance(block, ToolUseBlock):
639 |                     tool_calls.append({
640 |                         "id": block.id,
641 |                         "type": "function",
642 |                         "function": {
643 |                             "name": block.name,
644 |                             "arguments": json.dumps(block.input),
645 |                         },
646 |                     })
647 |             entry: dict[str, Any] = {"role": "assistant"}
648 |             if text_parts:
649 |                 entry["content"] = "".join(text_parts)
650 |             if tool_calls:
651 |                 entry["tool_calls"] = tool_calls
652 |             if "content" not in entry and "tool_calls" not in entry:
653 |                 entry["content"] = ""
654 |             oai_messages.append(entry)
655 |         else:
656 |             for block in msg.content:
657 |                 if isinstance(block, ToolResultBlock):
658 |                     oai_messages.append({
659 |                         "role": "tool",
660 |                         "tool_call_id": block.tool_use_id,
661 |                         "content": block.content,
662 |                     })
663 |                 elif isinstance(block, TextBlock):
664 |                     oai_messages.append({"role": msg.role, "content": block.text})
665 |     return oai_messages

683 | def _from_openai_response(raw: Any) -> ProviderResponse:
684 |     """Translate a raw OpenAI ``ChatCompletion`` → normalized ``ProviderResponse``.
685 | 
686 |     Enforces the R5 invariant: if ``message.tool_calls`` is non-empty, the
687 |     normalized ``stop_reason`` is ``TOOL_USE`` regardless of native
688 |     ``finish_reason`` (spike §5).
689 |     """
690 |     content: list[ContentBlock] = []
691 |     has_tool_use = False
692 | 
693 |     choices = getattr(raw, "choices", None) or []
694 |     if choices:
695 |         message = getattr(choices[0], "message", None)
696 |         if message is not None:
697 |             text = getattr(message, "content", None)
698 |             if text:
699 |                 content.append(TextBlock(text=text))
700 |             tool_calls = getattr(message, "tool_calls", None) or []
701 |             for tc in tool_calls:
702 |                 has_tool_use = True
703 |                 fn = getattr(tc, "function", None)
704 |                 tc_id = getattr(tc, "id", "") or ""
705 |                 name = getattr(fn, "name", "") if fn else ""
706 |                 args_str = getattr(fn, "arguments", "{}") if fn else "{}"
707 |                 try:
708 |                     args = json.loads(args_str) if isinstance(args_str, str) else dict(args_str)
709 |                 except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
710 |                     logger.warning(
711 |                         "OpenAI tool-call arguments were not valid JSON: %s; "
712 |                         "degrading to empty dict", args_str,
713 |                     )
714 |                     args = {}
715 |                 content.append(ToolUseBlock(id=tc_id, name=name, input=dict(args)))
716 | 
717 |     if has_tool_use:
718 |         stop_reason = StopReason.TOOL_USE
719 |     else:
720 |         finish_reason = ""
721 |         if choices:
722 |             finish_reason = getattr(choices[0], "finish_reason", "") or ""
723 |         stop_reason = (

725 |             if isinstance(finish_reason, str)
726 |             else StopReason.OTHER

729 |     raw_usage = getattr(raw, "usage", None)

742 | class OpenAIProvider:
743 |     """``LLMProvider`` adapter over the OpenAI Chat Completions API (P4-007).
744 | 
745 |     A boundary translator: normalized ``Message``/``ToolDef``/``system`` become
746 |     ``chat.completions.create`` kwargs, and the raw ``ChatCompletion`` becomes a
747 |     normalized ``ProviderResponse``. The provider owns no retry — loop-owned
748 |     retry reads ``classify_error`` and decides backoff + the budget-aware skip.
749 | 
750 |     The ``openai`` SDK is imported **lazily** in ``__init__`` so this module
751 |     imports without the package installed (tests that only exercise
752 |     ``AnthropicProvider`` are unaffected). Constructing an ``OpenAIProvider``
753 |     requires ``openai >= 1.0``.
754 |     """
755 | 
756 |     name = "openai"
757 | 
758 |     def __init__(self, *, base_url: str, api_key: str, timeout_s: float) -> None:
759 |         import openai as _openai
760 | 
761 |         self._openai_mod = _openai
762 |         # ``max_retries=0`` — loop-owned retry is authoritative (spike D-retry).
763 |         self._client = _openai.AsyncOpenAI(
764 |             base_url=base_url,
765 |             api_key=api_key,
766 |             timeout=httpx.Timeout(timeout_s, connect=30.0),
767 |             max_retries=0,
768 |         )
769 | 
770 |     async def messages_create(
771 |         self,
772 |         *,
773 |         model: str,
774 |         system: str,
775 |         messages: list[Message],
776 |         tools: list[ToolDef],
777 |         max_tokens: int,
778 |         temperature: float | None = None,
779 |         stop_sequences: list[str] | None = None,
780 |     ) -> ProviderResponse:
781 |         """One model turn via ``chat.completions.create``."""
782 |         kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
783 |             "model": model,
784 |             "max_tokens": max_tokens,
785 |             "messages": _to_openai_messages(messages, system),
786 |         }
787 |         if tools:
788 |             kwargs["tools"] = _to_openai_tools(tools)
789 |         if temperature is not None:
790 |             kwargs["temperature"] = temperature
791 |         if stop_sequences is not None:
792 |             kwargs["stop"] = stop_sequences
793 |         raw = await self._client.chat.completions.create(**kwargs)
794 |         return _from_openai_response(raw)
795 | 
796 |     async def complete(
797 |         self,
798 |         *,
799 |         model: str,
800 |         prompt: str,
801 |         max_tokens: int,
802 |         system: str | None = None,
803 |     ) -> str:
804 |         """One-shot text completion (insights / Haiku path)."""
805 |         oai_messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
806 |         if system:
807 |             oai_messages.append({"role": "system", "content": system})
808 |         oai_messages.append({"role": "user", "content": prompt})
809 |         raw = await self._client.chat.completions.create(
810 |             model=model, max_tokens=max_tokens, messages=oai_messages,
811 |         )
812 |         choices = getattr(raw, "choices", None) or []
813 |         if choices:
814 |             return getattr(choices[0].message, "content", None) or ""
815 |         return ""
816 | 
817 |     async def stream(self, **kwargs: Any) -> AsyncIterator[StreamDelta]:
818 |         """Token streaming (OPTIONAL in v1; D-stream). Not implemented for OpenAI."""
819 |         raise NotImplementedError(
820 |             "OpenAIProvider.stream is not implemented (ARC-011 D-stream)"
821 |         )
822 |         yield StreamDelta()  # pragma: no cover — makes this an async generator
823 | 
824 |     def estimate_cost(self, model: str, usage: Usage) -> float:
825 |         """Per-model USD cost for an OpenAI call.
826 | 
827 |         Uses a per-model pricing table with a gpt-4o-class default. Cache-blind
828 |         (parity with ``AnthropicProvider.estimate_cost``).
829 |         """
830 |         in_rate, out_rate = _OPENAI_PRICING.get(
831 |             model, (_OPENAI_DEFAULT_INPUT_USD_PER_TOKEN, _OPENAI_DEFAULT_OUTPUT_USD_PER_TOKEN),
832 |         )
833 |         return usage.input_tokens * in_rate + usage.output_tokens * out_rate
834 | 
835 |     def capabilities(self) -> ProviderCapabilities:
836 |         return ProviderCapabilities(
837 |             native_tool_use=True,
838 |             streaming=False,
839 |             system_prompt=True,
840 |             max_context_tokens=_OPENAI_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS,
841 |         )
842 | 
843 |     def classify_error(self, exc: Exception) -> ErrorClass:
844 |         """Classify an OpenAI SDK exception for loop-owned retry.
845 | 
846 |         ``transient`` mirrors the Anthropic decision: connection/timeout/server
847 |         errors plus HTTP status codes in ``_OPENAI_TRANSIENT_STATUS_CODES``
848 |         (429 / 500 / 502 / 503 / 504). Everything else is non-transient.
849 |         """
850 |         openai = self._openai_mod
851 |         if isinstance(
852 |             exc,
853 |             (
854 |                 openai.APITimeoutError,
855 |                 openai.APIConnectionError,
856 |                 openai.InternalServerError,
857 |             ),
858 |         ):
859 |             return ErrorClass(transient=True, status_code=None, retry_after_s=None)
860 |         if isinstance(exc, openai.APIStatusError):
861 |             status_code = getattr(exc, "status_code", None)
862 |             return ErrorClass(
863 |                 transient=status_code in _OPENAI_TRANSIENT_STATUS_CODES,
864 |                 status_code=status_code,
865 |                 retry_after_s=None,
866 |             )
867 |         return ErrorClass(transient=False, status_code=None, retry_after_s=None)
868 |

870 | # ── Provider router (P4-010) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
871 | 
872 | 
873 | class ProviderCapabilityMismatch(ValueError):
874 |     """Raised (ARC-011 P4-009) when a skill manifest's required capabilities
875 |     are not satisfied by the selected provider's ``capabilities()``.
876 | 
877 |     Fail-closed: a session whose skill demands (e.g.) native tool use but is
878 |     routed to a provider that lacks it must be rejected at session start,
879 |     before any LLM call — mirroring the codebase's existing fail-closed posture
880 |     (production-approval HMAC, command policy default-deny).
881 |     """
882 | 
883 | 
884 | # Capability requirements, expressed in the same terms as ProviderCapabilities.
885 | # Built from a skill manifest's ``LLMConfig.required_*`` fields. ``None`` means
886 | # "the manifest does not constrain this dimension" (skip the check).
887 | class RequiredCapabilities:
888 |     """Subset of :class:`ProviderCapabilities` a skill demands (P4-009)."""
889 | 
890 |     def __init__(
891 |         self,
892 |         *,
893 |         native_tool_use: Optional[bool] = None,
894 |         system_prompt: Optional[bool] = None,
895 |         max_context_tokens: Optional[int] = None,
896 |     ) -> None:
897 |         self.native_tool_use = native_tool_use
898 |         self.system_prompt = system_prompt
899 |         self.max_context_tokens = max_context_tokens
900 | 
901 |     @classmethod
902 |     def from_llm_config(cls, llm_cfg: Any) -> "RequiredCapabilities":
903 |         """Build from a skill manifest's ``LLMConfig`` (P4-009).
904 | 
905 |         Reads ``required_native_tool_use`` / ``required_system_prompt`` /
906 |         ``required_max_context_tokens``. Tolerates an older manifest that
907 |         lacks the fields (treats absent fields as unconstrained).
908 |         """
909 |         return cls(
910 |             native_tool_use=getattr(llm_cfg, "required_native_tool_use", None),
911 |             system_prompt=getattr(llm_cfg, "required_system_prompt", None),
912 |             max_context_tokens=getattr(llm_cfg, "required_max_context_tokens", None),
913 |         )
914 | 
915 |     def check(self, caps: ProviderCapabilities, provider_id: str) -> None:
916 |         """Raise :class:`ProviderCapabilityMismatch` if ``caps`` is insufficient."""
917 |         problems: list[str] = []
918 |         if self.native_tool_use and not caps.native_tool_use:
919 |             problems.append("native_tool_use")
920 |         if self.system_prompt and not caps.system_prompt:
921 |             problems.append("system_prompt")
922 |         if (
923 |             self.max_context_tokens is not None
924 |             and caps.max_context_tokens < self.max_context_tokens
925 |         ):
926 |             problems.append(
927 |                 f"max_context_tokens (need >= {self.max_context_tokens}, "
928 |                 f"have {caps.max_context_tokens})"
929 |             )
930 |         if problems:
931 |             raise ProviderCapabilityMismatch(
932 |                 f"provider {provider_id!r} does not satisfy the skill's required "
933 |                 f"capabilities: {', '.join(problems)}"
934 |             )
935 | 
936 | 
937 | def build_provider(
938 |     provider_id: str,
939 |     *,
940 |     settings_obj: Any = None,
941 |     required_capabilities: Optional[RequiredCapabilities] = None,
942 | ) -> LLMProvider:
943 |     """Construct a ``LLMProvider`` by id (ARC-011 P4-010 router).
944 | 
945 |     Maps a skill manifest's ``llm.provider`` (``"anthropic"`` / ``"openai"``) to
946 |     a concrete provider instance, reading API credentials from ``settings``.
947 |     The orchestrator calls this per-session (or at init for the default) so each
948 |     skill can select its provider declaratively. Anthropic remains the default
949 |     for ML skills that do not declare a provider override.
950 | 
951 |     The ``settings_obj`` is injectable for tests; production passes ``None`` and
952 |     the function falls back to the singleton ``src.config.settings``.
953 |     """
954 |     from src.config import secret_value
955 | 
956 |     if settings_obj is None:
957 |         from src.config import settings as _settings
958 | 
959 |         settings_obj = _settings
960 | 
961 |     if provider_id == "anthropic":
962 |         provider: LLMProvider = AnthropicProvider(
963 |             base_url=settings_obj.anthropic_base_url,
964 |             api_key=secret_value(settings_obj.anthropic_auth_token) or "",
965 |             timeout_s=settings_obj.anthropic_api_timeout_s,
966 |         )
967 |     elif provider_id == "openai":
968 |         key = getattr(settings_obj, "openai_api_key", None)
969 |         provider = OpenAIProvider(
970 |             base_url=settings_obj.openai_base_url,
971 |             api_key=secret_value(key) if key is not None else "",
972 |             timeout_s=settings_obj.openai_api_timeout_s,
973 |         )
974 |     else:
975 |         raise ValueError(
976 |             f"unknown LLM provider {provider_id!r}; expected 'anthropic' or 'openai'"
977 |         )
978 | 
979 |     # ARC-011 P4-009: fail-closed capability check. When the caller supplies
980 |     # the skill's required capabilities, validate them against the provider's
981 |     # advertisement before returning — so a mismatch fails the session at
982 |     # start, before any LLM call. Default provider construction (orchestrator
983 |     # init) passes no requirements and skips the check.
984 |     if required_capabilities is not None:
985 |         required_capabilities.check(provider.capabilities(), provider_id)
986 |     return provider

1 | #!/usr/bin/env python3
  2 | """Prompt-engineering eval scorer (ARC-011 P4-014).
  3 | 
  4 | Scores a candidate prompt against a labeled eval set and emits an
  5 | ``ITERATION_RESULT:`` JSON marker carrying the W11 anti-forgery nonce
  6 | (``server_nonce``, read from ``AUTORESEARCH_SESSION_NONCE``).
  7 | 
  8 | The scorer is deliberately deterministic: it derives a composite score from a
  9 | hash of the prompt text so the e2e test (P4-016) gets reproducible metrics
 10 | without an external LLM scorer. A real deployment would replace the scoring
 11 | body with a call to ``--scorer-url``; the marker contract (nonce + fields) stays
 12 | the same.
 13 | 
 14 | Usage::
 15 | 
 16 |     .venv/bin/python eval/run.py --prompt prompt.yaml --eval eval_set.jsonl
 17 | """
 18 | from __future__ import annotations
 19 | 
 20 | import argparse
 21 | import hashlib
 22 | import json
 23 | import os
 24 | import sys
 25 | 
 26 | 
 27 | def _score_prompt(prompt_text: str, eval_examples: list[dict]) -> dict:
 28 |     """Derive deterministic metrics from the prompt text + eval set size.
 29 | 
 30 |     A real scorer calls an external endpoint; this deterministic stub hashes the
 31 |     prompt to produce a stable composite score in [0, 1), precision, and a cost
 32 |     estimate. The gates (passes_min_precision, within_cost_budget) are derived
 33 |     from the score so the orchestrator's phase logic exercises real decisions.
 34 |     """
 35 |     h = int(hashlib.sha256(prompt_text.encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
 36 |     composite = (h % 10000) / 10000.0  # [0, 1)
 37 |     precision = ((h >> 16) % 10000) / 10000.0  # [0, 1)
 38 |     n = len(eval_examples)
 39 |     mean_cost_usd = 0.01 * n  # $0.01 per eval example
 40 | 
 41 |     passes_min_precision = precision >= 0.6
 42 |     within_cost_budget = mean_cost_usd <= 0.50
 43 | 
 44 |     return {
 45 |         "status": "completed",
 46 |         "primary_metric": round(composite, 6),
 47 |         "metric_name": "composite_eval_score",
 48 |         "precision": round(precision, 6),
 49 |         "passes_min_precision": passes_min_precision,
 50 |         "within_cost_budget": within_cost_budget,
 51 |         "mean_cost_usd": round(mean_cost_usd, 4),
 52 |         "n_eval_examples": n,
 53 |         "composite_eval_score": round(composite, 6),
 54 |         # The skill's own gates ARE its training gates (review C4: downstream
 55 |         # consumers — decision inference, promotion gates — read this field
 56 |         # on every iteration).
 57 |         "training_gates_passed": passes_min_precision and within_cost_budget,
 58 |     }
 59 | 
 60 | 
 61 | def main() -> int:
 62 |     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Score a candidate prompt")
 63 |     parser.add_argument("--prompt", required=True, help="Path to the prompt file")
 64 |     parser.add_argument("--eval", required=True, help="Path to the eval set (JSONL)")
 65 |     args = parser.parse_args()
 66 | 
 67 |     # Read the prompt.
 68 |     try:
 69 |         with open(args.prompt, encoding="utf-8") as f:
 70 |             prompt_text = f.read()
 71 |     except OSError as exc:
 72 |         print(f"eval_error: cannot read prompt: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
 73 |         _emit(status="eval_error", error=str(exc))
 74 |         return 1
 75 | 
 76 |     # Read the eval set (JSONL — one JSON object per line).
 77 |     eval_examples: list[dict] = []
 78 |     try:
 79 |         with open(args.eval, encoding="utf-8") as f:
 80 |             for line in f:
 81 |                 line = line.strip()
 82 |                 if line:
 83 |                     eval_examples.append(json.loads(line))
 84 |     except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
 85 |         print(f"eval_error: cannot read eval set: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
 86 |         _emit(status="eval_error", error=str(exc))
 87 |         return 1
 88 | 
 89 |     # Score.
 90 |     metrics = _score_prompt(prompt_text, eval_examples)
 91 |     _emit(**metrics)
 92 |     return 0
 93 | 
 94 | 
 95 | def _emit(**fields: object) -> None:
 96 |     """Emit an ``ITERATION_RESULT:`` JSON line with the anti-forgery nonce."""
 97 |     nonce = os.environ.get("AUTORESEARCH_SESSION_NONCE", "")
 98 |     payload = dict(fields)
 99 |     payload["server_nonce"] = nonce
100 |     # Ensure required fields are present (the parser checks for them).
101 |     payload.setdefault("status", "completed")
102 |     payload.setdefault("primary_metric", 0.0)
103 |     payload.setdefault("metric_name", "composite_eval_score")
104 |     payload.setdefault("n_eval_examples", 0)
105 |     print("ITERATION_RESULT: " + json.dumps(payload), flush=True)
106 | 
107 | 
108 | if __name__ == "__main__":
109 |     sys.exit(main())

1 | """``LLMProvider`` protocol + normalized value types + ``AnthropicProvider``
  2 | (ARC-011 P1-001 / P1-002).
  3 | 
  4 | This module adopts the X-005 LLM-provider normalization spike §4 *verbatim*
  5 | (``docs/adr/ARC-011-llm-provider-spike.md``) as the canonical contract every
  6 | provider implementation must satisfy: ``messages_create`` (main agentic path),
  7 | ``complete`` (one-shot insights/Haiku path), an optional ``stream``,
  8 | ``estimate_cost`` (→ P1-003), ``capabilities`` (→ P4-009 / router P4-010), and
  9 | ``classify_error`` (→ loop-owned retry, R4).
 10 | 
 11 | P1-002 extracts ``AnthropicProvider`` — the 1:1 SDK adapter — into this module.
 12 | The orchestrator (P1-002) consumes ``ProviderResponse`` (normalized
 13 | ``StopReason``/``ContentBlock``/``Usage``) and holds its conversation as
 14 | ``list[Message]``. The provider translates at the SDK boundary only, so the
 15 | Anthropic wire format is byte-identical to pre-refactor and the X-002 parity
 16 | suite is preserved.
 17 | 
 18 | Design decisions recorded by the spike and baked in here:
 19 | 
 20 | * **Anthropic-shaped normalized types** (spike §4 note). ``ToolUseBlock.input``
 21 |   is a ``dict`` (Anthropic shape; OpenAI's JSON-string ``function.arguments``
 22 |   is parsed by the provider), ``ToolResultBlock`` is the Anthropic tool-result
 23 |   block, and ``ToolDef`` matches the ``AGENT_TOOLS`` shape. This keeps
 24 |   ``AnthropicProvider`` a 1:1 wrapper and preserves the parity suite.
 25 | * **Loop-owned retry (R4 / D-retry).** The protocol exposes
 26 |   ``classify_error``; the loop owns backoff + the budget-aware skip
 27 |   (``orchestrator.py`` ``_call_llm_with_retry``). ``ErrorClass.transient`` is
 28 |   the signal. Retry does NOT live in the provider — the budget-aware skip
 29 |   depends on session wall-clock state (``remaining_budget_s``), which is loop
 30 |   policy, not provider state.
 31 | * **Phase-contract enforcement is loop-level (R5 / §5).** The provider surfaces
 32 |   a normalized ``StopReason``; the loop reads ``StopReason.END_TURN`` to trigger
 33 |   phase continuation. The defensive invariant *"tool calls present ⇒
 34 |   TOOL_USE, regardless of the native finish_reason"* (Gemini can report
 35 |   ``STOP`` with function calls present) is the provider's responsibility —
 36 |   enforced in ``AnthropicProvider._from_sdk_response``.
 37 | * **Not ``@runtime_checkable``.** ``isinstance`` against a ``Protocol`` only
 38 |   checks attribute presence (false confidence on signatures). This is a
 39 |   typing-time contract; consumers accept it as a typed parameter.
 40 | 
 41 | Three places where the spike §4 draft was incomplete (resolved in P1-001, the
 42 | only deviations from a literal copy — see inline comments):
 43 | 
 44 | 1. The draft references ``ContentBlock`` (in ``ProviderResponse.content``) and
 45 |    ``StreamDelta`` (in ``stream()``) without defining them.
 46 | 2. The draft's ``Message{role, content: list[Block]}`` does not match the live
 47 |    orchestrator, which builds messages with ``content: str`` (user prompts) and
 48 |    ``content: list[block]`` (assistant / tool-result turns).
 49 | """
 50 | 
 51 | from __future__ import annotations
 52 | 
 53 | import json
 54 | import logging
 55 | from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
 56 | from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
 57 | from enum import Enum
 58 | from typing import Any, Optional, Protocol
 59 |

 61 | import httpx

 63 | logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 64 | 
 65 | # Claude pricing constants (Sonnet 3.5 baseline) — moved here from
 66 | # ``orchestrator.py`` (P1-002). Referenced by ``AnthropicProvider.estimate_cost``
 67 | # and by the orchestrator's pre-spend budget gate + post-call accounting. The
 68 | # flat-rate model ignores cache tokens (parity with pre-refactor; per-model
 69 | # pricing is P1-003).
 70 | _CLAUDE_INPUT_USD_PER_TOKEN = 3.0 / 1_000_000
 71 | _CLAUDE_OUTPUT_USD_PER_TOKEN = 15.0 / 1_000_000
 72 | _CLAUDE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS = 8192
 73 | 
 74 | # HTTP status codes the pre-refactor ``_call_claude_with_retry`` treated as
 75 | # transient (rate-limit / overloaded / bad-gateway family). Used by
 76 | # ``AnthropicProvider.classify_error``.
 77 | _TRANSIENT_STATUS_CODES = frozenset({429, 502, 503, 529})
 78 | 
 79 | 
 80 | class StopReason(str, Enum):
 81 |     """Normalized reason the model stopped generating (R5-critical).
 82 | 
 83 |     Provider mapping (spike §3.3 / §5):
 84 | 
 85 |     * Anthropic ``end_turn`` / OpenAI ``stop`` / Gemini ``STOP`` → ``END_TURN``
 86 |     * ``tool_use`` / OpenAI ``tool_calls`` / function-calls-present → ``TOOL_USE``
 87 |     * ``max_tokens`` / OpenAI ``length`` / Gemini ``MAX_TOKENS`` → ``MAX_TOKENS``
 88 |     * ``stop_sequence`` → ``STOP_SEQUENCE``
 89 |     * anything else (``pause_turn``, ``refusal``, ``content_filter``, …) → ``OTHER``
 90 | 
 91 |     R5 invariant: a provider MUST return ``TOOL_USE`` whenever the response
 92 |     carries tool/function calls, even if the native ``finish_reason`` says
 93 |     ``STOP`` (Gemini quirk). The loop keys off ``END_TURN`` for phase
 94 |     continuation (``orchestrator.py`` ``run``).
 95 |     """
 96 | 
 97 |     END_TURN = "end_turn"
 98 |     TOOL_USE = "tool_use"
 99 |     MAX_TOKENS = "max_tokens"
100 |     STOP_SEQUENCE = "stop_sequence"
101 |     OTHER = "other"
102 | 
103 |

107 | 
108 |     ``cache_read_tokens`` / ``cache_write_tokens`` default to 0 and are unused
109 |     today (the orchestrator reads only input/output, ``orchestrator.py``
110 |     ``run``); additive so P1-003 can capture cache-aware cost without breaking
111 |     parity.
112 |     """
113 | 
114 |     input_tokens: int

117 |     cache_write_tokens: int = 0

def _fallback_score(prompt_text: str, eval_examples: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """Deterministic offline fallback (no network / no scorer_url).

    Preserved from the original P4-014 stub so unit tests and demo mode stay
    reproducible. Flagged with ``scorer: fallback`` so downstream consumers
    never mistake it for a real LLM judgment.
    """
    h = int(hashlib.sha256(prompt_text.encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
    composite = (h % 10000) / 10000.0  # [0, 1)
    precision = ((h >> 16) % 10000) / 10000.0  # [0, 1)
    n = len(eval_examples)
    mean_cost_usd = 0.01 * n  # $0.01 per eval example

    passes_min_precision = precision >= 0.6
    within_cost_budget = mean_cost_usd <= 0.50

    return {
        "status": "completed",
        "primary_metric": round(composite, 6),
        "metric_name": "composite_eval_score",
        "precision": round(precision, 6),
        "passes_min_precision": passes_min_precision,
        "within_cost_budget": within_cost_budget,
        "mean_cost_usd": round(mean_cost_usd, 4),
        "n_eval_examples": n,
        "composite_eval_score": round(composite, 6),
        # The skill's own gates ARE its training gates (review C4: downstream
        # consumers — decision inference, promotion gates — read this field
        # on every iteration).
        "training_gates_passed": passes_min_precision and within_cost_budget,
        "scorer": "fallback",
    }


def _try_remote_scorer(
    prompt_text: str,
    eval_examples: list[dict],
    scorer_url: str,
    timeout_s: float = 15.0,
) -> dict | None:
    """POST the candidate to an external scorer; None on any failure.

    Contract: POST {prompt, examples} -> {composite_eval_score, precision}.
    Fail-open to the next scorer in the chain (never crash the eval).
    """
    try:
        import urllib.request

        payload = json.dumps(
            {"prompt": prompt_text, "examples": eval_examples}
        ).encode("utf-8")
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            scorer_url,
            data=payload,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
            method="POST",
        )
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout_s) as resp:
            body = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
        composite = float(body.get("composite_eval_score", body.get("score", 0.0)))
        precision = float(body.get("precision", composite))
        n = len(eval_examples)
        mean_cost_usd = round(0.01 * n, 4)
        passes = precision >= 0.6
        within = mean_cost_usd <= 0.50
        return {
            "status": "completed",
            "primary_metric": round(composite, 6),
            "metric_name": "composite_eval_score",
            "precision": round(precision, 6),
            "passes_min_precision": passes,
            "within_cost_budget": within,
            "mean_cost_usd": mean_cost_usd,
            "n_eval_examples": n,
            "composite_eval_score": round(composite, 6),
            "training_gates_passed": passes and within,
            "scorer": "remote",
        }
    except Exception:
        return None


def _try_openai_judge(
    prompt_text: str,
    eval_examples: list[dict],
    model: str | None = None,
) -> dict | None:
    """Score via OpenAI chat completions as an LLM judge; None if unavailable.

    Reads OPENAI_BASE_URL / OPENAI_API_KEY from env. Scores each example on a
    0..1 rubric by asking the judge whether the candidate prompt would elicit
    the expected answer, then averages. Fail-open (None) on missing creds or
    any transport error so the chain falls through to the fallback scorer.
    """
    base_url = os.environ.get("OPENAI_BASE_URL", "https://api.openai.com/v1").rstrip("/")
    api_key = os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY", "")
    if not api_key or not eval_examples:
        return None
    model = model or os.environ.get("OPENAI_JUDGE_MODEL", "gpt-4o-mini")
    try:
        import urllib.request

        scores: list[float] = []
        for ex in eval_examples[:50]:  # cap judge cost per run
            user_msg = (
                "Candidate system prompt:\n---\n" + prompt_text[:4000] + "\n---\n"
                f"User input: {ex.get('input', '')}\n"
                f"Expected answer: {ex.get('expected', '')}\n"
                "On a 0..1 scale, how likely is the candidate prompt to elicit "
                "the expected answer? Reply with ONLY a number like 0.85."
            )
            body = json.dumps(
                {
                    "model": model,
                    "messages": [
                        {
                            "role": "system",
                            "content": "You are a strict prompt-quality judge. Reply with only a number 0..1.",
                        },
                        {"role": "user", "content": user_msg},
                    ],
                    "max_tokens": 16,
                    "temperature": 0,
                }
            ).encode("utf-8")
            req = urllib.request.Request(
                base_url + "/chat/completions",
                data=body,
                headers={
                    "Content-Type": "application/json",
                    "Authorization": "Bearer " + api_key,
                },
                method="POST",
            )
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30) as resp:
                raw = json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
            text = raw["choices"][0]["message"]["content"].strip()
            m = re.search(r"0?\.\d+|[01](?:\.0+)?", text)
            scores.append(max(0.0, min(1.0, float(m.group(0)) if m else 0.5)))
        composite = sum(scores) / len(scores)
        # Precision proxy: fraction of examples scoring >= 0.7.
        precision = sum(1 for s in scores if s >= 0.7) / len(scores)
        n = len(eval_examples)
        mean_cost_usd = round(0.002 * min(n, 50) + 0.001 * n, 4)
        passes = precision >= 0.6
        within = mean_cost_usd <= 0.50
        return {
            "status": "completed",
            "primary_metric": round(composite, 6),
            "metric_name": "composite_eval_score",
            "precision": round(precision, 6),
            "passes_min_precision": passes,
            "within_cost_budget": within,
            "mean_cost_usd": mean_cost_usd,
            "n_eval_examples": n,
            "composite_eval_score": round(composite, 6),
            "training_gates_passed": passes and within,
            "scorer": "openai-judge:" + model,
        }
    except Exception:
        return None


def _score_prompt(
    prompt_text: str,
    eval_examples: list[dict],
    *,
    scorer_url: str | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """Real scorer chain: remote scorer -> OpenAI judge -> offline fallback.

    The marker contract (nonce + required fields) is unchanged regardless of
    which link in the chain produces the metrics; the winning link is recorded
    in the ``scorer`` field for auditability.
    """
    if scorer_url:
        remote = _try_remote_scorer(prompt_text, eval_examples, scorer_url)
        if remote is not None:
            return remote
    judge = _try_openai_judge(prompt_text, eval_examples)
    if judge is not None:
        return judge
    return _fallback_score(prompt_text, eval_examples)

# Code Refactor Research

You are a **code refactor research agent**. Iterate on a Python target file,
validate each candidate with syntax + lint + test gates, and promote the best.

## How iterations work

1. **Edit** `refactor_target.py` in the session workspace (one meaningful change).
2. **Run**: `.venv/bin/python eval/run.py --target refactor_target.py --tests tests_target.jsonl`
3. The scorer emits `ITERATION_RESULT:` JSON with `primary_metric`
   (composite refactor score), `tests_pass`, `no_perf_regression`,
   `test_pass_rate`, `complexity_drop_pct`, and `server_nonce` (anti-forgery —
   copied from `AUTORESEARCH_SESSION_NONCE`).
4. Keep improvements (update `best_refactor_target.py`), revert the rest.

## Phases

- **baseline_capture**: run the scorer once on the bootstrap target.
- **mechanical_refactors**: rename, extract, dead-code removal, one at a time.
- **validation**: full syntax + lint + test re-check of the winner.
- **promotion_proposal**: propose the winning file for promotion.

## Promotion

Winner promotes via `file_path` to `configs/code-refactor/<subject>_<variant>.py`.
Scopes: `development` then `production` (production requires approval).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Code-refactor eval scorer (P0-2).

Validates a candidate Python file with syntax + pyflakes-style lint + a
JSONL test ledger, then emits an ``ITERATION_RESULT:`` JSON marker carrying
the W11 anti-forgery nonce (``server_nonce``).

Offline by design: no network, no repo checkout needed. A real deployment
wraps the repo's own pytest/benchmark harness; the marker contract stays.

Usage::

    .venv/bin/python eval/run.py --target refactor_target.py
        --tests tests_target.jsonl [--baseline complexity.json]
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import ast
import hashlib
import json
import os
import sys


def _lint_score(tree: ast.AST, source: str) -> tuple[float, int]:
    """Lightweight lint: unused imports + long functions penalty in [0,1]."""
    issues = 0
    imported: set[str] = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
            for a in node.names:
                imported.add((a.asname or a.name).split(".")[0])
        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
            for a in node.names:
                if a.name != "*":
                    imported.add((a.asname or a.name).split(".")[0])
    names_used: set[str] = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
            names_used.add(node.id)
    issues += len(imported - names_used)
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef):
            length = len(node.body)
            if length > 30:
                issues += (length - 30) // 10 + 1
    # Long lines penalty (cap contribution).
    long_lines = sum(1 for ln in source.splitlines() if len(ln) > 100)
    issues += min(long_lines, 10)
    score = max(0.0, 1.0 - 0.05 * issues)
    return score, issues


def _test_pass_rate(target_text: str, test_ledger: list[dict]) -> float:
    """Ledger entries: {needle, must_present(true)/must_absent(false)}."""
    if not test_ledger:
        return 1.0
    passed = 0
    for t in test_ledger:
        needle = str(t.get("needle", ""))
        want = bool(t.get("must_present", True))
        found = needle in target_text
        if found == want:
            passed += 1
    return passed / len(test_ledger)


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Score a refactor candidate")
    parser.add_argument("--target", required=True, help="Candidate Python file")
    parser.add_argument("--tests", default="", help="Test ledger JSONL")
    parser.add_argument("--baseline", default="", help="Baseline JSON (complexity)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    try:
        with open(args.target, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            target_text = f.read()
    except OSError as exc:
        print(f"eval_error: cannot read target: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        _emit(status="eval_error", error=str(exc))
        return 1

    try:
        tree = ast.parse(target_text)
        syntax_ok = True
    except SyntaxError as exc:
        print(f"build_failed: syntax error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        _emit(status="build_failed", error=str(exc))
        return 1

    ledger: list[dict] = []
    if args.tests:
        try:
            with open(args.tests, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                for line in f:
                    line = line.strip()
                    if line:
                        ledger.append(json.loads(line))
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
            print(f"eval_error: cannot read tests: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
            _emit(status="eval_error", error=str(exc))
            return 1

    lint_score, lint_issues = _lint_score(tree, target_text)
    pass_rate = _test_pass_rate(target_text, ledger)
    h = int(hashlib.sha256(target_text.encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
    # Complexity proxy: function count + line count, hashed jitter keeps the
    # offline demo discriminative between candidates.
    fn_count = sum(1 for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef))
    lines = max(1, len(target_text.splitlines()))
    complexity = fn_count * 3 + lines / 20.0
    baseline_cplx = complexity
    if args.baseline:
        try:
            baseline_cplx = float(json.load(open(args.baseline))["complexity"])
        except Exception:
            baseline_cplx = complexity
    drop_pct = (
        round(100.0 * (baseline_cplx - complexity) / max(baseline_cplx, 1e-9), 2)
        if baseline_cplx
        else 0.0
    )
    jitter = ((h >> 32) % 1000) / 1000.0  # [0,1) deterministic tiebreak
    composite = round(
        0.5 * pass_rate + 0.3 * lint_score + 0.2 * min(1.0, max(0.0, drop_pct / 20.0))
        + 0.001 * jitter,
        6,
    )
    tests_pass = pass_rate >= 1.0
    no_perf_regression = syntax_ok and lint_issues <= 10
    metrics = {
        "status": "completed",
        "primary_metric": composite,
        "metric_name": "composite_refactor_score",
        "composite_refactor_score": composite,
        "test_pass_rate": round(pass_rate, 6),
        "tests_pass": tests_pass,
        "no_perf_regression": no_perf_regression,
        "complexity_drop_pct": drop_pct,
        "lint_issues": lint_issues,
        "n_tests": len(ledger),
        "training_gates_passed": tests_pass and no_perf_regression,
        "scorer": "offline-refactor",
        "refactor_applied": True,
        "baseline_metrics": True,
        "full_validation": tests_pass,
        "promotion_proposal": False,
    }
    with open("eval_result.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(metrics, f)
    _emit(**metrics)
    try:
        with open("complexity.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump({"complexity": complexity}, f)
    except OSError:
        pass
    return 0


def _emit(**fields: object) -> None:
    nonce = os.environ.get("AUTORESEARCH_SESSION_NONCE", "")
    payload = dict(fields)
    payload["server_nonce"] = nonce
    payload.setdefault("status", "completed")
    payload.setdefault("primary_metric", 0.0)
    payload.setdefault("metric_name", "composite_refactor_score")
    print("ITERATION_RESULT: " + json.dumps(payload), flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

schema_version: research_skill.v1
id: db-config-tuning
version: 0.1.0
category: optimization
display_name: "Database Configuration Tuning"
description: "Tune an offline-simulated DB config for throughput/latency and promote the winner."

llm:
  provider: anthropic
  primary_model: claude-sonnet-4-20250514
  insight_model: claude-haiku-4-20250514
  max_output_tokens: 8192
  system_prompt: SKILL.md

workspace:
  session_path_template: "runs/{skill_id}/{subject_id}/{variant}"

subjects:
  static:
    - { id: postgres16, label: "Postgres 16 (simulated)" }
variants:
  static: [tpcb, oltp_read_only]

param_schema:
  type: object
  additionalProperties: false
  properties:
    target_latency_ms: { type: integer, minimum: 1, default: 10 }
    bench_duration_s: { type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 3600, default: 60 }
  required: []

metric_schema:
  primary:
    field: primary_metric
    label: "TPS @ target latency"
    direction: higher_is_better
    format: ".1f"
  gates:
    - { field: p99_within_slo, label: "p99 SLO", kind: boolean_badge }
    - { field: no_regression, label: "No Regr", kind: boolean_badge }
  chart_series:
    - { field: tps, label: "TPS" }
    - { field: p99_latency_ms, label: "p99 ms", axis: right }
  iteration_table_columns:
    - { field: primary_metric, label: "TPS" }
    - { field: p99_within_slo, label: "SLO", kind: icon }
    - { field: no_regression, label: "Regr", kind: icon }
    - { field: bench_duration_s, label: "Dur" }
  goal: optimize

decision_vocabulary:
  base: [keep, discard, improve, unknown]
  extensions: []
  success_values: [keep, improve]

phase_plan:
  - id: baseline_capture
    label: "Baseline capture"
    min_iterations: 1
    max_iterations: 2
    evidence_keys: [baseline_tps]
  - id: memory_tuning
    label: "Memory tuning"
    min_iterations: 1
    max_iterations: 12
    evidence_keys: [memory_knob_swept]
    next_action: "Sweep shared_buffers, work_mem, effective_cache_size."
  - id: validation
    label: "Validation"
    min_iterations: 1
    max_iterations: 5
    evidence_keys: [soak_test_passed]
  - id: promotion_proposal
    label: "Promotion proposal"
    min_iterations: 1
    max_iterations: 2
    evidence_keys: [promotion_proposal]
    stagnation_exempt: true
    next_action: "Prepare a development-scoped promotion proposal."
phase_advancement:
  mode: declarative

command_policy:
  allowed_python: [".venv/bin/python", "./.venv/bin/python"]
  allowed_scripts:
    - eval/run.py
    - bootstrap.py
  allowed_executables: [cp, cat, jq]
  copyable_files: [db_config.yaml, best_db_config.yaml]
  readable_files: [db_config.yaml, best_db_config.yaml, bench_result.json]
  forbidden_tokens: ["|", "||", "&&", ";", "&"]
  forbidden_substrings: ["`", "$", ">", "<", "\\n", "\\r"]
  secret_markers: [.env, /proc/, /run/secrets, authorization, bearer, credential, id_rsa, password, secret, token]

output_parser:
  format: json_marker
  iteration_marker: "ITERATION_RESULT:"
  nonce_field: server_nonce
  require_signed_metrics: true
  required_fields: [status, primary_metric, metric_name, p99_within_slo]
  failure_statuses: [crash, timeout, failed, error, bench_failed]
  fallback:
    read_results_file: bench_result.json
    marker_dir_template: "{workspace_root}/runs/{skill_id}/{subject_id}/{variant}/"

preflight: []

trial_identity:

blocker_classification:

structured_hpo:

# Database Configuration Tuning

You are a **DB config tuning agent** (offline simulation). Edit `db_config.yaml`,
run the bench, and promote the highest-TPS config that meets the p99 SLO.

## How iterations work

1. **Edit** `db_config.yaml` (one knob: `shared_buffers_mb`, `work_mem_mb`,
   `effective_cache_size_mb`, `max_connections`).
2. **Run**: `.venv/bin/python eval/run.py --config db_config.yaml --target-latency-ms 10`
3. Marker carries `primary_metric` (TPS), `p99_latency_ms`, `p99_within_slo`,
   `no_regression`, `server_nonce`.
4. Keep winners in `best_db_config.yaml`.

## Phases

- **baseline_capture** → **memory_tuning** → **validation** → **promotion_proposal**.

## Promotion

`file_path` to `configs/db/<subject>_<variant>.yaml`. Production needs approval.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""DB-config bench simulator (P0-2). Offline deterministic TPS model."""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse, hashlib, json, os
def _emit(**fields):
    p = dict(fields); p["server_nonce"] = os.environ.get("AUTORESEARCH_SESSION_NONCE", "")
    p.setdefault("status", "completed"); p.setdefault("primary_metric", 0.0); p.setdefault("metric_name", "tps")
    print("ITERATION_RESULT: " + json.dumps(p), flush=True)
def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--config", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--target-latency-ms", type=float, default=10.0)
    ap.add_argument("--baseline-tps", type=float, default=0.0)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    try:
        import yaml
        cfg = yaml.safe_load(open(a.config, encoding="utf-8")) or {}
    except Exception:
        try:
            cfg = json.load(open(a.config, encoding="utf-8"))
        except Exception as exc:
            _emit(status="bench_failed", error=str(exc)); return 1
    sb = float(cfg.get("shared_buffers_mb", 128)); wm = float(cfg.get("work_mem_mb", 4))
    ec = float(cfg.get("effective_cache_size_mb", 512)); mc = float(cfg.get("max_connections", 100))
    h = int(hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(cfg, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
    jitter = ((h >> 16) % 200 - 100) / 100.0
    tps = 800 + 2.0 * sb + 15.0 * wm + 0.2 * ec - 0.5 * max(0, mc - 200) + jitter * 5
    tps = max(50.0, round(tps, 1))
    p99 = round(max(1.0, 40.0 - sb / 64.0 - wm / 8.0 + max(0, mc - 100) / 50.0), 2)
    slo = p99 <= a.target_latency_ms * 3
    no_regr = (a.baseline_tps <= 0) or (tps >= 0.95 * a.baseline_tps)
    m = {"status": "completed", "primary_metric": tps, "metric_name": "tps", "tps": tps,
        "p99_latency_ms": p99, "p99_within_slo": slo, "no_regression": no_regr,
        "bench_duration_s": 60, "training_gates_passed": slo and no_regr,
        "scorer": "offline-bench", "memory_knob_swept": True, "baseline_tps": True,
        "soak_test_passed": slo, "promotion_proposal": False}
    open("bench_result.json", "w", encoding="utf-8").write(json.dumps(m))
    _emit(**m)
    return 0
if __name__ == "__main__":
    import sys; sys.exit(main())

"""Legacy alias registry — ``model_type ↔ skill_id`` (ARC-011 P2-019).

The back-compat bridge between the legacy ``model_type`` field
(``direction``/``volatility``/``rl``) and the canonical ``skill_id``
(``ml-direction``/``ml-volatility``/``ml-rl``). Legacy API callers that send
``model_type`` (ARC-011 §10 guarantee #5) are auto-translated to ``skill_id``
here; the orchestrator and SkillRuntime reach for ``skill_id`` only.

Design note (P1-007 house style):

* The canonical manifest skill ids (``ml-direction`` etc.) are distinct from the
  legacy on-disk primer directory names (``direction-autotuner`` etc.) the
  transitional ``_SKILL_IDENTITY`` map in ``skill_runtime.py`` uses. This module
  owns the ``model_type ↔ manifest skill_id`` mapping; the primer-dir mapping
  is transitional and retired by P2-021. The two are reconciled here so callers
  can pass either form.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

#: Legacy ``model_type`` → canonical manifest ``skill_id``.
_MODEL_TYPE_TO_SKILL_ID: dict[str, str] = {
    "direction": "ml-direction",
    "volatility": "ml-volatility",
    "rl": "ml-rl",
}

#: Reverse lookup (canonical manifest ``skill_id`` → legacy ``model_type``).
_SKILL_ID_TO_MODEL_TYPE: dict[str, str] = {v: k for k, v in _MODEL_TYPE_TO_SKILL_ID.items()}


def model_type_to_skill_id(model_type: str) -> str:
    """Translate a legacy ``model_type`` to its canonical ``skill_id``.

    Known legacy values map to their canonical skill ids; any other non-empty
    value is already a canonical ``skill_id`` and is returned unchanged
    (``skill_id`` is the universal vocabulary — non-legacy skills are their own
    ``model_type`` alias). Empty string stays empty.
    """
    if not model_type:
        return ""
    return _MODEL_TYPE_TO_SKILL_ID.get(model_type, model_type)


def skill_id_to_model_type(skill_id: str) -> str:
    """Translate a canonical ``skill_id`` back to its legacy ``model_type``.

    Known canonical ids map to their legacy short names; any other non-empty
    id is its own ``model_type`` alias (empty string stays empty).
    """
    if not skill_id:
        return ""
    return _SKILL_ID_TO_MODEL_TYPE.get(skill_id, skill_id)


def is_known_model_type(model_type: str) -> bool:
    """Whether ``model_type`` maps to a Phase-2 skill (excludes ``pipeline``)."""
    return model_type in _MODEL_TYPE_TO_SKILL_ID

@router.get("/skills/{skill_id}/leaderboard")
async def get_skill_leaderboard(
    skill_id: str,
    limit: int = Query(default=20, ge=1, le=100, title="Limit"),
):
    """Cross-session leaderboard for one skill (P0-4).

    Aggregates every session recorded for the skill (by ``skill_id`` and its
    legacy ``model_type`` alias) that produced a best metric, sorted by the
    skill's declared primary-metric direction. The comparison surface the
    Dashboard lacked: best metric, iterations spent, cost, subject/variant.
    """
    manifest = _get_or_404(skill_id)
    metric_dump = manifest.metric_schema.model_dump(exclude_none=True, mode="json")
    primary = metric_dump.get("primary", {}) or {}
    direction = primary.get("direction", "higher_is_better")

    rows: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    seen_ids: set[str] = set()
    if _store is not None:
        # Non-legacy skills are their own model_type alias; legacy skills also
        # match on the short name, so query both shapes and merge by id.
        model_type_aliases = {skill_id, skill_id_to_model_type(skill_id)}
        for alias in sorted(model_type_aliases):
            if not alias:
                continue
            for session in await _store.list_sessions(model_type=alias, limit=500):
                rid = str(session.get("id") or "")
                if not rid or rid in seen_ids:
                    continue
                if session.get("best_metric") is None:
                    continue
                seen_ids.add(rid)
                rows.append(
                    {
                        "research_id": rid,
                        "subject_id": session.get("subject_id")
                        or session.get("instrument"),
                        "variant": session.get("variant") or session.get("timeframe"),
                        "tag": session.get("tag"),
                        "status": session.get("status"),
                        "best_metric": session.get("best_metric"),
                        "metric_name": session.get("metric_name"),
                        "best_iteration": session.get("best_iteration"),
                        "iterations": session.get("effective_iteration_count")
                        or session.get("best_iteration")
                        or 0,
                        "total_api_cost_usd": session.get("total_api_cost_usd") or 0.0,
                        "started_at": session.get("started_at"),
                        "completed_at": session.get("completed_at"),
                    }
                )

    rows.sort(
        key=lambda r: (r.get("best_metric") is None, r.get("best_metric") or 0.0),
        reverse=(direction == "higher_is_better"),
    )
    total = len(rows)
    return {
        "skill_id": skill_id,
        "metric": {
            "field": primary.get("field", "primary_metric"),
            "label": primary.get("label", "Primary metric"),
            "direction": direction,
            "format": primary.get("format", ".4f"),
        },
        "items": rows[:limit],
        "total": total,
    }

class WebhookPromotionTarget:
    """Promote by POSTing the winning config to an HTTP endpoint (P1-3).

    Implements the file-shaped ``PromotionTarget`` protocol so the whole
    ``ConfigPromoter`` gate/metadata/rollback machinery keeps working: every
    write lands atomically in a local provenance tree
    (``<workspace_root>/promotions/...``), and the *primary* config write is
    additionally delivered to the declared webhook endpoint with an
    ``Idempotency-Key`` and optional Bearer auth. Delivery failures raise
    ``WebhookDeliveryError`` so ``confirm`` surfaces them (fail-closed) —
    a promotion that was never delivered must not report success.

    Serves both ``promotion_target.kind: webhook`` manifests and
    ``kind: registry_api`` manifests (a registry register-endpoint is a
    webhook delivery with an auth secret).
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        endpoint: str,
        auth_env_var: str | None = None,
        timeout_s: float = 10.0,
        retries: int = 2,
        local_root: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if not endpoint:
            raise ValueError("WebhookPromotionTarget requires an endpoint")
        self.endpoint = endpoint
        self.auth_env_var = auth_env_var
        self.timeout_s = timeout_s
        self.retries = max(0, retries)
        self.local_root = local_root or os.path.join(
            settings.workspace_root, "promotions"
        )
        #: Primary config paths derived by ``target_path`` — only these are
        #: delivered to the endpoint; sidecars/rollback snapshots stay local.
        self._primary_paths: set[str] = set()
        #: Last delivery outcome (for audit/tests).
        self.last_delivery: dict[str, Any] | None = None

    # ── PromotionTarget protocol: local provenance paths ──────────────────

    def target_path(
        self,
        *,
        model_type: str,
        instrument: str,
        timeframe: str,
    ) -> str:
        path = os.path.join(
            self.local_root,
            str(model_type or "skill").replace("/", "-"),
            f"{instrument}_{timeframe}.yaml",
        )
        self._primary_paths.add(path)
        return path

    def metadata_sidecar_path(
        self,
        target_path: str,
        iteration: int,
        *,
        scope: str = "development",
    ) -> str:
        path = Path(target_path)
        return str(
            path.with_name(
                f"{path.name}.{scope}-promotion.iter-{iteration}.json"
            )
        )

    def rollback_snapshot_path(
        self,
        *,
        target_path: str,
        research_id: str,
        iteration: int,
    ) -> str:
        path = Path(target_path)
        safe_research_id = "".join(
            char if char.isalnum() or char in {"-", "_"} else "_"
            for char in research_id
        )
        return str(
            path.with_name(
                f"{path.name}.development-rollback."
                f"{safe_research_id}.iter-{iteration}.yaml"
            )
        )

    def rollback_metadata_sidecar_path(
        self, target_path: str, promotion_id: int
    ) -> str:
        path = Path(target_path)
        return str(
            path.with_name(
                f"{path.name}.development-rollback.promotion-{promotion_id}.json"
            )
        )

    async def write(self, path: str, content: str) -> None:
        """Atomic local write; deliver to the endpoint on the primary path."""
        await asyncio.to_thread(_atomic_write_text, path, content)
        if path in self._primary_paths:
            await self.deliver(path, content)

    # ── Webhook delivery ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

    async def deliver(self, path: str, content: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """POST the promoted config to the endpoint (retries, idempotent key).

        Raises :class:`WebhookDeliveryError` after the final failed attempt —
        fail-closed so the caller records the promotion as failed rather than
        pretending the remote side received it.
        """
        import hashlib
        from datetime import datetime, timezone

        import httpx

        idempotency_key = hashlib.sha256(
            f"{path}:{content}".encode()
        ).hexdigest()[:32]
        headers = {
            "Content-Type": "application/json",
            "Idempotency-Key": idempotency_key,
        }
        token = os.environ.get(self.auth_env_var, "") if self.auth_env_var else ""
        if token:
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
        payload = {
            "target_path": path,
            "config": content,
            "promoted_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
            "endpoint": self.endpoint,
        }

        attempts = self.retries + 1
        last_error: Exception | None = None
        for attempt in range(1, attempts + 1):
            try:
                async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=self.timeout_s) as client:
                    resp = await client.post(self.endpoint, json=payload, headers=headers)
                if 200 <= resp.status_code < 300:
                    self.last_delivery = {
                        "endpoint": self.endpoint,
                        "status_code": resp.status_code,
                        "idempotency_key": idempotency_key,
                        "attempt": attempt,
                        "response": resp.text[:512],
                    }
                    return self.last_delivery
                last_error = RuntimeError(
                    f"webhook {self.endpoint} answered HTTP {resp.status_code}: "
                    f"{resp.text[:200]}"
                )
                if resp.status_code < 500:
                    break  # 4xx will not improve with retries
            except (httpx.TimeoutException, httpx.TransportError) as exc:
                last_error = exc
            if attempt < attempts:
                await asyncio.sleep(0.5 * attempt)
        raise WebhookDeliveryError(
            f"webhook delivery to {self.endpoint} failed after "
            f"{attempts} attempt(s): {last_error}"
        )


class WebhookDeliveryError(RuntimeError):
    """A webhook promotion delivery failed after all retries (fail-closed)."""

    ``kind: registry_api`` manifests (a registry register-endpoint is a
    webhook delivery with an auth secret).

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        endpoint: str,
        auth_env_var: str | None = None,
        timeout_s: float = 10.0,
        retries: int = 2,
        local_root: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        if not endpoint:
            raise ValueError("WebhookPromotionTarget requires an endpoint")
        self.endpoint = endpoint
        self.auth_env_var = auth_env_var
        self.timeout_s = timeout_s
        self.retries = max(0, retries)
        self.local_root = local_root or os.path.join(
            settings.workspace_root, "promotions"
        )
        #: Primary config paths derived by ``target_path`` — only these are
        #: delivered to the endpoint; sidecars/rollback snapshots stay local.
        self._primary_paths: set[str] = set()
        #: Last delivery outcome (for audit/tests).
        self.last_delivery: dict[str, Any] | None = None

    # ── PromotionTarget protocol: local provenance paths ──────────────────

    def target_path(
        self,
        *,
        model_type: str,
        instrument: str,
        timeframe: str,
    ) -> str:
        path = os.path.join(
            self.local_root,
            str(model_type or "skill").replace("/", "-"),
            f"{instrument}_{timeframe}.yaml",
        )
        self._primary_paths.add(path)
        return path

    def metadata_sidecar_path(
        self,
        target_path: str,
        iteration: int,
        *,
        scope: str = "development",
    ) -> str:
        path = Path(target_path)
        return str(
            path.with_name(
                f"{path.name}.{scope}-promotion.iter-{iteration}.json"
            )
        )

    def rollback_snapshot_path(
        self,
        *,
        target_path: str,
        research_id: str,
        iteration: int,
    ) -> str:
        path = Path(target_path)
        safe_research_id = "".join(
            char if char.isalnum() or char in {"-", "_"} else "_"

            path.with_name(
                f"{path.name}.development-rollback."
                f"{safe_research_id}.iter-{iteration}.yaml"
            )
        )

    def rollback_metadata_sidecar_path(
        self, target_path: str, promotion_id: int
    ) -> str:
        path = Path(target_path)
        return str(
            path.with_name(
                f"{path.name}.development-rollback.promotion-{promotion_id}.json"
            )
        )

    async def write(self, path: str, content: str) -> None:
        """Atomic local write; deliver to the endpoint on the primary path."""

def _confirm_audit_metadata(payload: PromotionScopeRequest) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Metadata recorded in the ``promotion.confirm`` audit event (W18 / AC #4).

    ``actor_id`` (the authenticated API caller's identity) is written
    automatically by ``record_api_audit_event``; this records the *named human
    approver* from the request body so the audit row carries full provenance.
    """
    metadata: dict[str, Any] = {"scope": payload.scope}
    if payload.approval is not None:
        metadata["approver"] = payload.approval.approver
        metadata["approval_method"] = payload.approval.method
    return metadata


async def _promoter_for_session(research_id: str):
    """Pick the promoter for a session (P1-3).

    Default: the injected ``_promoter`` (singleton, file target). When the
    session's skill declares a ``webhook`` / ``registry_api`` promotion target
    with an endpoint (and the registry is wired), a per-request
    ``ConfigPromoter`` backed by a ``WebhookPromotionTarget`` is built so the
    manual API path delivers like the auto-promote path does. Anything that
    cannot be resolved (unknown skill, missing endpoint, stubbed registry)
    falls back to the injected promoter — never fails the request here.
    """
    if _registry is None or _store is None:
        return _promoter
    try:
        session = await _store.get_session(research_id)
    except Exception:
        return _promoter
    if not session:
        return _promoter
    skill_id = session.get("skill_id") or ""
    if not skill_id:
        model_type = session.get("model_type") or ""
        if model_type:
            from src.core.legacy_alias import model_type_to_skill_id

            skill_id = model_type_to_skill_id(model_type)
    if not skill_id:
        return _promoter
    try:
        manifest = _registry.get(skill_id)
    except Exception:
        return _promoter
    primary = getattr(getattr(manifest, "promotion_target", None), "primary", None)
    kind = getattr(primary, "kind", None)
    if kind not in ("webhook", "registry_api"):
        return _promoter
    endpoint = getattr(primary, "endpoint", None)
    if not endpoint:
        return _promoter
    from src.core.config_promoter import ConfigPromoter
    from src.core.promotion_target import WebhookPromotionTarget

    target = WebhookPromotionTarget(
        endpoint=endpoint,
        auth_env_var=getattr(primary, "auth_secret", None) or None,
        timeout_s=getattr(primary, "timeout_s", 10.0),
        retries=getattr(primary, "retries", 2),
    )
    return ConfigPromoter(_store, target=target)

Covers: local provenance writes + endpoint delivery on the primary path only,
idempotency key + bearer auth, retry-then-fail-closed behavior, manifest
schema acceptance of ``kind: webhook``, runtime wiring for webhook and
registry_api kinds, and the API-layer per-session promoter selection.
